page: Amazon Web Services hpc7a.24xlarge is an x86_64 high-performance computing instance powered by a dedicated AMD EPYC 9R14 processor running on the Nitro hypervisor. It delivers 48 physical cores and 48 vCPUs with single-threaded core execution at 3.7 GHz. The system includes 768.0 GB of DDR5 memory clocked at 5 GHz, providing a generous 16.0 GB of RAM per core, along with an integrated 300 Gbps network interface. The instance does not include local disk storage or hardware GPUs, requiring external storage attachments for persistent filesystem needs.

Benchmark results demonstrate exceptional multi-core throughput and memory subsystem capacity. Stress-ng multi-core testing reached 147,294.74, placing in the top tier, paired with strong single-core results of 3,075.88. Large-block memory tests yielded top-tier throughput of 695.05 GB/s read and 347.3 GB/s write, while cached small-block read speeds attained 7,105.26 GB/s. Parallel tasks scale effectively, demonstrated by multi-threaded bzip3 decompression achieving 636.8 GB/s and Clang compilation reaching a top-tier score of 59,439.0. In-memory data throughput is equally elevated, showing 122.53 million operations per second on Redis SET tests.

Hardware trade-offs center around the absence of local NVMe storage and lack of hyperthreading, which prioritizes deterministic physical core execution and predictability over total thread count. The 16:1 memory-to-core ratio and 300 Gbps networking favor distributed memory scaling and data-intensive simulation. This architectural configuration is suited for tightly coupled compute clusters, finite element analysis, computational fluid dynamics, large in-memory databases, and distributed technical computing workloads.
description: Amazon Web Services hpc7a.24xlarge is an x86_64 high-performance computing instance based on AMD EPYC 9R14 processors on the Nitro hypervisor. It features 48 dedicated physical cores running at 3.7 GHz with one thread per core, 768.0 GB of high-speed DDR5 memory (16.0 GB per core), and a 300 Gbps network interface. It includes no local storage or GPUs. The architecture yields top-tier multi-threaded processing and memory bandwidth, reaching 695.05 GB/s read throughput on large blocks and 122.53 million operations per second on Redis SET benchmarks. Extended instruction set support includes AVX-512 extensions such as VNNI and BF16. The high memory density and elevated interconnect bandwidth make it well-suited for distributed scientific simulations, computational fluid dynamics, Clang compilation clusters, and large in-memory data processing.
